questions.question: The three-tier system of local government does NOT include the _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Village Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was a committee originally appointed by the Government of India to examine the working of the Community Development Programme and the National Extension Service.
 
• The committee was formed on **16th January 1957**.
 
• **Balwant Rai Mehta** was the Chairman of this committee.
 
• The establishment of a **3-tier Panchayati Raj system** is one of the main recommendations of this committee.
 
• The 3-tier system recommended by this committee is:
 
 
• **Gram Panchayat **at the village level.
 
• **Panchayat Samiti** at the block level.
 
• **Zila Parishad** at the district level.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Other important recommendations** **of the** **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** **are**:

 
• The Panchayat Samiti should be the executive body while the Zila Parishad should be the advisory, coordinating, and supervisory body.
 
• The District Collector should be the Chairman of the Zila Parishad.

questions.question: In which battle was Napoleon defeated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **3** i.e __**Waterloo**__.

 
• Napoleon Bonaparte was the **Emperor of the French**.

 
 
• He ruled France twice.
 
• The first reign was from 1804 to 1814.
 
• The second reign was in 1815.
 
• He led many successful campaigns during the** French Revolutionary Wars**.
 
• Napoleon Bonaparte is considered one of the greatest commanders in history.
 
• He fought more than 70 battles, losing only seven, mostly at the end.
 
 
 
• Important Battles won by Napoleon Bonaparte are:
 
 
• Battle of Montenotte
 
• Battle of Ceva.
 
• Battle of Lodi.
 
• Battle of Borghetto.
 
• Battle of Mount Tabor.
 
• Battle of Borodino.
 
• **Battle of Arcole** in 1796
 
• **Battle of Jena** in 1806
 
• **Battle of Ligny **in 1815.
 
 
 
• Napoleon was defeated in the Battle of Waterloo.
 
 
• The Battle of Waterloo was fought in **1815 in Belgium**.
 
• Battle fought between Napoleon's French Army and a coalition led by the Duke of Wellington and Marshal Blücher. 
 
• Battle of Waterloo resulted in:
 
 
• End of the Seventh Coalition.
 
• Final defeat of Napoleon.
 
• End of the Napoleonic Wars.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a multicellular animal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 
• Amoeba is a **unicellular organism** that has the ability to alter its shape.

 
 
• Grouped under the **Kingdom Protista**.
 
• Commonly found in water bodies like **ponds and lakes**.
 
• Based on records amoeboid organism was produced in 1755 by** August Johann Rösel von Rosenhof**.
 
• The structure of Amoeba consists of cytoplasm, plasma membrane, and nucleus.
 
• Locomotion is possible through** pseudopodia**.
 
• Amoeba reproduces through asexual means, such as** binary fission**.
 
• Amoeba follows holozoic nutrition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/712ce093d85ed6951919e9d37f7b2a83f5a2b404d9871c3bff97bfd7668e347b.png]

questions.question: Which of the following is the hardest substance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option** 2** i.e __**Diamond**__.

 
• Diamond is an allotrope of carbon.
 
 
• Diamond is a crystalline carbon.
 
• Diamond is the **hardest naturally occurring substance** found on Earth.
 
• The hardness of diamond is **10 Mohs**.
 
• Diamond has been used as decorative items since ancient times.
 
• The refractive index of diamond is **2.42**.
 
• There is only one industrial-scale diamond mine in India located at **Panna**, Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Coal **is an amorphous carbon.
 
 
• Diesel oil is produced by the hydrogenation of coal.
 
 
 
• **Iron** is a chemical element with atomic number 26.
 
 
• When iron rusts, its weight increases.
 
• The purest form of Iron is called Wrought Iron.
 
• The impure iron is called Pig Iron.
 
 
 
• **Silver** is a chemical element with atomic number 47.
 
 
• Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals.

questions.question: The deltas of the Mahanadi and the Godavari are rich in ______ soil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahanadi** and **Godavari River Deltas** are a basin of the deposit that drains a large landmass into the Bay of Bengal.

 
 
• The deltas of the Mahanadi and the Godavari are rich in** alluvial soils**.
 
• The upper part of the Mahanadi delta plain is heavily populated.
 
 
 
• Alluvial soil is the most extensive soil type in India.
 
 
• It covers about 43% of the total area in India.
 
• Alluvial soils divided into the **Khadar** (new alluvium) and the **Bhangar** (old alluvium).
 
• Light grey to Ash grey in colour.
 
• Alluvial soils are **rich in potash** and poor in nitrogen and organic matter.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23357598984e01688c191ffff6a811a9bf2c17d9a2a19cbf8930189ce4b9586a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Black soil
 
 
 
• Also called **Regur soil.**
 
• Volcanic origin.
 
• The best soil for** cotton cultivation.**
 
• High water-retaining capacity is an advantage.
 
 
 
 

 Forest soil
 
 
 
• Found in **high rainfall areas.**
 
• Suitable for the plantation of tea, coffee, and spices in Kerala, Karnataka, and the North-eastern states of India.
 
• Soil is acidic in nature.
 
 
 
 

 Arid soil
 
 
 
• Found in **arid and semi-arid regions**.
 
• High salt and low humus content.
 
• Support very few crops like Barley, Jowar, Bajra.

questions.question: Which country gave universal suffrage since the century?

• **Australia** became the first country in the world to give most women the right to vote and the right to stand for the Commonwealth Parliament in 2002.
 
• **India** agreed to the principle of universal suffrage in 1947.
